CVF's EXTENSIONS/CVF_v1.6_AGENT_PLATFORM/cvf-web/src/lib/agent-tools.tsx was opened directly this pass (not just its test file): it begins with 'use client' (a browser-rendered React component), and its url_fetch tool calls validateUrl() (protocol-only check: http/https) then a literal BLOCKED_PATTERNS regex array against the raw URL string, then browser-native fetch(url). sharedMechanismsView.label: Deterministic outbound-network egress control (server-side proxy vs. browser-side client tool -- different trust boundaries)
sharedMechanismsView.description: QM's src/egress-authz-main.ts implements an AUTHORIZATION DECISION endpoint (buildEgressAuthzServer/checkStatus/onRequest): given a capability token and a target host, it resolves the hostname via DNS, re-checks the resolved IP against a BlockList (link-local/loopback/cloud-metadata ranges) and policy, then returns HTTP 200 with an x-egress-upstream-address header or HTTP 403 -- it does not itself forward CONNECT byte traffic; the actual proxying component (if any) was not read and is not claimed to exist in this file. AGW's examples/traffic-egress-proxy demonstrates a full HTTP CONNECT proxy with hostname allowlisting via TLS SNI (no decryption) or optional TLS termination for HTTP-policy inspection. Both are SERVER-SIDE components mediating outbound traffic from a service the operator controls.
sharedMechanismsView.existingCvfOwnerEvidence: EXTENSIONS/CVF_v1.6_AGENT_PLATFORM/cvf-web/src/lib/agent-tools.tsx read directly this pass (lines 1-280): the file begins with 'use client' (a browser-rendered React component, not a CVF server); its url_fetch tool runs validateUrl() (protocol-only check) then a literal BLOCKED_PATTERNS regex array against the raw URL string, then calls browser-native fetch(url) -- executing in the end user's own browser. agent-tools.test.tsx:140-173 tests this same client-side string-blocklist logic.
sharedMechanismsView.missingCvfLink: QM and AGW's mechanisms are SERVER-SIDE egress controls with a DNS-lookup step available to them because they run on infrastructure the operator controls. CVF's url_fetch tool is a CLIENT-SIDE (browser) fetch with no equivalent DNS-lookup step available to it in that execution context -- a browser cannot be made to 'recheck a resolved IP' the way a server-side proxy can, because the browser's own network stack (subject to the browser's own SSRF-relevant protections, CORS, and same-origin policy) performs the resolution, not CVF code. The original audit's framing (treating this as a directly portable 'add resolved-IP recheck to agent-tools.tsx' gap) does not hold: there is no comparable seam in a 'use client' component to insert a server-side DNS recheck.
sharedMechanismsView.expectedBenefit: None established this pass for a direct port of QM/AGW's server-side mechanism into agent-tools.tsx's client-side execution context. If CVF later adds a SERVER-SIDE outbound-fetch capability (distinct from this browser-side tool), QM's decide()-function shape (resolve-then-recheck) would be a relevant reference pattern for that different consumer.
sharedMechanismsView.nextAction: No action against agent-tools.tsx specifically; if a future CVF work order introduces a server-side agent-initiated outbound-fetch capability, evaluate QM's decide() pattern against that new consumer at that time.
sharedMechanismsView.reopenTrigger: A named CVF consumer introduces a server-side (not browser 'use client') agent-initiated outbound-fetch capability

sharedMechanismsView.label: Deterministic shell-command safety policy with de-obfuscation
sharedMechanismsView.description: QM's src/policy/command-policy.ts implements a full command-policy engine: org-floor denylist rules (recursive delete, force-push, destructive SQL, fork bombs, pipe-to-shell) plus scope-composable custom rules, and -- the substantial part -- a scannableCommand() normalizer that recursively unwraps nested shell constructs (command substitution $()/`` `` `, heredocs that run an interpreter, piped producer/consumer pairs, here-strings, simple variable expansion, SQL client -c/-e payload extraction for psql/mysql/sqlite3/etc.) before running regex rules against the fully de-obfuscated scannable text, specifically to prevent quoting/substitution tricks from hiding a destructive pattern from a naive regex scan.

sharedMechanismsView.label: Non-extractable shared-credential proxy (broker pattern)
sharedMechanismsView.description: QM's skills-seed/use-shared-credential/SKILL.md documents (and names a corresponding core-side broker endpoint, not itself opened) a pattern where the agent never receives a raw shared secret: it names a credential slug, method, URL and headers, and a core-side broker stamps the real secret onto the outbound request, returning only the upstream status/body envelope. The broker enforces per-credential host/method/path-prefix allowlisting and records every use for attribution/billing/abuse review. A parallel path handles Git smart-HTTP remotes without ever placing a token in a clone URL.
sharedMechanismsView.existingCvfOwnerEvidence: NOT_FOUND in this bounded pass. CVF's provider API-key handling (route.ts apiKeyMap, lines ~270-278 per the prior AGW-UC-02 pass) reads keys directly from server-side environment variables and uses them directly server-side for CVF's own first-party provider calls; this is a different shape of problem (CVF's server already holds the keys and never hands them to an agent) rather than QM's shape (an agent-facing broker so a semi-trusted agent process never sees an org's shared third-party secret it would otherwise need to hold locally).
